Andrew, an affable grad student researching Dostoevsky, has the perfect med-student boyfriend, but one night at the laundromat he meets a handsome stranger named Jack. Andrew is immediately smitten as Jack removes his shirt to add it to the wash. Intrigued, Andrew starts dating Jack. Only problem is, hidden by his mop of gorgeous hair, Jack has the Mark of the Beast (666), and his Dad is…well, the Devil.

description: Take your place at a beastsly dinner with "Brainpeople." Taking place in a not-so-distant future, the sounds of a war-torn Los Angeles fill the air. She has done this every year, and the two troubled women she has invited stand to take home $20,000 each if they can make it through dessert. Over the course of the evening, her dark purpose is revealed to be much more than a mere commemoration, as tensions rise, identities transform, and the main dish proves not to be the only thing with claws.

description: The Screwtapes Letters, the provocative and wickedly witty theatrical adaptation of the C.S. Lewis novel about spiritual warfare from a demon’s point of view, will be presented at The Touhill Performing Arts Center. The Screwtapes Letter is now in its fifth month of an open ended run at New York City’s Westside Theatre with McLean as Screwtape. McLean will take a short break from the New York production to perform the role in St. Louis. The New York Times writes “The Devil has rarely been given his due more perceptively and eruditely”; New York Post calls it “As entertaining as it is thought-provoking”; The Screwtape Letters is “Wickedly witty…one hell of a good show!” raves the Wall Street Journal. Elle writes “Brilliant…Hilarious wit” and The Associated Press calls the production “Devilishly funny…Lewis’ philosophical insights are cleverly conveyed!” The Chicago Sun-Times hails The Screwtape Letters as “Smart, sizzling entertainment!” and National Review says that the production is “Pure genius…an outstanding piece of work.” Prior to its current New York engagement it was a hit at Chicago’s Mercury Theatre where it ran for six months and at The Shakespeare Theatre in Washington, D.C. where it played for ten sold out weeks. Last fall it delighted capacity houses in San Francisco, Phoenix, Louisville, Chattanooga, Ft. Lauderdale, Houston and Austin. Adapted for the stage by Jeffrey Fiske and Max McLean, The Screwtapes Letters, runs 90 minutes without intermission. In this inverted moral universe set in an office in hell, God is called the “Enemy” and the devil is referred to as “Our Father below.” The play follows His Abysmal Sublimity Screwtape, played by Max McLean (2009 recipient of Chicago’s Jeff Award for Solo Performance), and his creature-demon secretary, Toadpipe, as they train an apprentice demon, Wormwood, on how to entice the mind of a human “patient” toward damnation. The actors’ combined skills wheedle their unsuspecting soul down the “soft, gentle path to hell.” The book’s success as a piercing insight into humanity’s bent toward evil is due to Lewis’ lucid capacity to make his readers squirm in self recognition. When first published in 1942, it brought immediate fame to this little-known Oxford don, including the cover of Time Magazine. The Screwtape Letters is still one Lewis’ most influential works, along with such other classics as The Chronicles of Narnia (including The Lion,The Witch and The Wardrobe), The Great Divorce and Mere Christianity. Lewis dedicated it to his close friend J. R. R. Tolkien who had expressed to Lewis that delving too deeply into the craft of evil would have consequences. Lewis admitted as much when he wrote “Though I had never written anything more easily, I never wrote with less enjoyment . . . though it was easy to twist one’s mind into the diabolical attitude, it was not fun, or not for long. The work into which I had to project myself while I spoke through Screwtape was all dust, grit, thirst, and itch. Every trace of beauty, freshness, and geniality had to be excluded.” Scenic Design is by Cameron Anderson, Costumes by Michael Bevins, Lighting Design by Jesse Klug, and Original Music and Sound Design by John Gromada.
venue: Blanche M. Touhill Performing Arts Center
title: The Screwtape Letters

Normal 0 false false false EN-US X-NONE X-NONE MicrosoftInternetExplorer4 The Gasparilla International Film Festival (GIFF) has chosen March 24-27 as the dates for its fifth-annual film showcase. Experiencing huge success in 2010, the film festival continues to grow into the entertainment and economic blockbuster that the Tampa Bay area had hoped it would be. Despite the tough economic climate, the shorter 2010 festival brought in an impressive number of local residents and national visitors to the area that totaled more than 1,000 film enthusiasts per day. This year's new president and advisory board anticipate even more growth for GIFF's fifth anniversary.

The Gasparilla International Film Festival is a celebration of independent film held annually in Tampa, Florida. The festival seeks to create a unique film showcase that has lasting and cultural impact on the Tampa Bay community - and the film community at large. The festival will be held at venues in and around Ybor City - Tampa's National Historic Landmark District, Latin Quarter, Downtown Tampa, Tampa Theatre, Tampa’s Fireman’s Museum, University of Tampa, Channelside Cinemas, and Studio @620 in St. Petersburg.

With venues on the water and in the historic district, VIP parties in the "Old" buildings with a "New" vibe, and opportunities to get up close and personal with celebrities and filmmakers the Gasparilla International Film Festival offers a Florida, experience you won't soon forget.

Celebrate the spirit of independent film with industry panels and discussions, and opening and closing night events. Please visit www.gasparillafilmfestival.com for information about festival dates, film schedules, and after-parties! Volunteers are needed to make the Gasparilla International Film Festival successful in more ways than one, so if you want to help make a difference, you can also volunteer!
title: 2011 Gasparilla International Film Festival

description:
This theatrical experience features two sets of characters, the colorful Cirques (circus perfromers) and monochromatic Urbains (urbanites). As the adventure unfolds, the show jumps back and forth between the two worlds, showing the contrasts as well as the similarities. Some of the world's most talented performers bring this spectacle to life through acting, pantomime, dance, juggling, acrobatics, tight rope and trapeze acts, live music and more. Journey into the unique world of Cirque du Soleil with a cast of colorful characters, including Les Cons, The Green Bird, The Titan and The Dancers.

From a group of 20 street performers at its beginning in 1984, Cirque du Soleil is now a major Quebec-based organization providing high-quality artistic entertainment. The company has more than 4,000 employees from over 40 different countries, including 1,000 performing artists. Cirque du Soleil has brought wonder and delight to almost 90 million spectators in over 200 cities on five continents. In 2009, Cirque du Soleil will present 20 shows simultaneously throughout the world.

description: "New York destroyed; it's the end of the world. You might as well go home to die. I just heard it on the radio."-–Indianapolis woman, October 30, 1938. Part radio play, part live theatre event, five actors recreate the most famous radio broadcast of all time, H.G. Wells' "The War of the Worlds." Be a part of the studio audience for the live event inspired by Orson Welles and the Mercury Theater, that rattled the nation on October 30, 1938. The script by Howard Koch (who also won an Academy Award for the screenplay of "Casablanca") is as eerily thrilling today as it was 67 years ago. Hear the story that caused a near-panic from coast to coast and led thousands to believe that an interplanetary conflict had begun with a Martian invasion of New Jersey and New York, eventually spurred legislation banning the "news" format from radio drama for years following.

The show covers everything from the the poetry of Suzanne Somers to Tommy Lee's romance tips, offering a look into the unintentionally hilarious lives of celebrities. Praised by the New York Times, the hit show also took home the 2009 Drama Desk Award for Best Unique Theatrical Experience. This three-week engagement offers family friendly shows on Fridays and Sundays, and an adult-flavored show on Thursdays.
title: "Celebrity Autobiography"

description: See quirky, adult-oriented puppet shows by area puppeteers. 18 and older.
title: Adult Puppet Slam

description: In this play by George Bernard Shaw, Candida seems the perfect woman - smart, spirited, loving, and capable. She is married to Morell, an eloquent and passionate preacher. But when she brings home a fervent young poet who falls in love with her, a battle ensues to secure her heart. Which man will win her? Or will they both lose? This witty ode to love, faith, beauty, and strong women truly defines the word “classic.”
title: 'Candida' at the Two River Theater

description: "Intimate Apparel," Pulitzer Prize-winner Lynn Nottage's vivid tale, is set among the bustle of New York in the early part of the 20th century. Esther, a talented African-American seamstress, crafts stunning undergarments for women from the brothels to the Upper East Side. Shimmering with vital and memorable characters, this is a powerful and moving tale of romance, independence, acceptance, and what lies just under our outer appearances.
title: 'Intimate Apparel' at the Two River Theater

description: Making great art is never easy. Making it in perfect harmony might just be impossible. When one member of an esteemed string quartet is fired days before the most important performance of their career, the others must quickly find a replacement. Personalities clash, tensions rise, and the musicians grapple with how far they will go to achieve excellence. This play—about the shockingly difficult dynamics of a string quartet—has been called "vibrant", "astounding", and "truly remarkable." "Opus," written by Michael Hollinger and directed by Matthew Arbour, is a passionate, smart, funny and moving story that resonates with the creative artist in all of us.
title: 'Opus' at Two River Theater

description: Charlie Schulman's uproariously dark and delightfully clever new comedy about a playwright and a theater critic locked in a mortal battle of wits and aspirations is set to premiere at the New Jersey Repertory Company in Long Brach starring Warren Kelley and Brad Frazier, directed by Dana Benningfield. Opening night with a reception will be at 8 p.m. Saturday, Sept. 25. For more information, visit NJ Rep's website.
title: 'Character Assassins' at NJ Rep

description:
The winner of 8 Tony Awards, including Best Musical and told by Duncan Sheik and Steven Sater through what Entertainment Weekly called “the most gorgeous Broadway score this decade,” "Spring Awakening" explores the journey from adolescence to adulthood with poignancy and passion you will never forget.

The landmark musical "Spring Awakening" is an electrifying fusion of morality, sexuality, and rock n' roll that is exhilarating audiences across the nation like no other musical in years. Join this group of late 19th century German students on their passage, as they navigate teenage self-discovery and coming of age anxiety in a powerful celebration of youth and rebellion in the daring, remarkable "Spring Awakening."
title: 'Spring Awakening' at the State Theatre

description: William Shakespeare’s dreamlike comedy of starry-eyed lovers, mischief-making fairies and a magical forest is brought to life by the BAMA Theatre Company (alumni from the Alabama Shakespeare Festival). Not the fluffy fairy tale you thought, eight actors magically morph into everything from a caustic duke to a mischievous sprite, all out of one suitcase. This Alabama company takes a breath at the top and doesn’t exhale until the curtain comes down. These performances take place at the Crossroads Theatre, 7 Livingston Ave
title: 'A Midsummer Night’s Dream' at the Crossroads

description: Naughty, funny, dark, and romantic, this is a spectacular, twisty, and intoxicating revue of the work of singer-songwriter Jacques Brel. Over half a century after they were written, Brel’s songs retain their edgy vibe in a show The New York Times calls “a potent mixture of romanticism and cynicism, world-weariness and jaunty whimsy.” If you've seen it before, you've never seen it like this. If you've never seen it, it's about time!
title: 'Jacques Brel Is Alive and Well and Living in Paris' at Two River Theater

description:
The spirit of Tony Hunting is alive and well at the SRYC today. The Yacht Club is in preparation to relive its past with a vaudeville show to be presented by its members in September. The show will include musical numbers of the Vaudeville genre, as well as dance and comedy skits.

It will be presented on Friday and Saturday, September 24 and 25, for members of the community as guests of the Club. It will begin each evening at 7 p.m. with refreshments available, followed by the show starting at 7:30 PM. Show tickets are $10. Reservations can be made by calling 732-747-9873 and asking for Lee or leaving a message.

The Twin Rivers of New Jersey and their neighboring communities have a storied history. Of equal historic note – and probably less known – is the history of what is now called The Shrewsbury River Yacht Club.
title: Vaudeville Theatre at the Shrewsbury River Yacht Club

description:
(Credit: Advertiser library photo)

Every first Friday of the month, Downtown and Chinatown galleries, shops and restaurants open their doors in the evening for various displays, exhibits, performances and other entertainment.

A free gallery walking map is available at all participating sites, or by visiting firstfridayhawaii.com
title: First Friday

description:
Hazzah! The Minnesota Renaissance Festival is back for another year of great food, entertainment, crafts and foul humor fit for a king. Enjoy delicious and interesting foods including scotch eggs, turkey legs, the queens apples and the kings nuts —sharing with friends is recommended so you can enjoy twice as much.

While you are snacking on delicious treats, take in some of the entertainment happening both on stages and right on the woodchip streets surrounding you. A few of our favorites are the pickle vendors (beware, they will throw them at you), Puke & Snot, and for the not easily offended, Vegetable Justice.

The Ren Fest is open 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. Saturdays and Sunday thru October 3rd. For more information on festival events and themes, visit the official website.
title: Minnesota Renaissance Festival

description:
You don't have to go to NYC or LA to see a quality, professional theater performance—some of the best shows are right here in the TC! Don't miss one of the most glamorous and entertaining theater events of the year as dozens of professional theatres and the artists who make it happen are honored at the 2010 Ivey Awards.

Besides general reserved seating at the State Theatre, several VIP packages are also offered including pre and post party celebrations. Visit the Ivey Awards ticket page for more information and to purchase.
title: The 2010 Ivey Awards

description:
In a unique marriage of theater and the sustainable foods movement, Mixed Precipitation presents Jacques Offenbach's masterpiece Tales of Hoffman. It is an operetta that will be touring to 14 community garden spaces around the Twin Cities during the 2010 harvest season each Saturday and Sunday in the late afternoon.

Their irreverent treatment of this operetta is perfect for opera lovers, gardeners, kids, and foodies alike. There will also be artfully created locally sourced food samplings by Chef Nick Schneider that will be prepared fresh and served during the performance to translate events of the story.

For more information on locations, please visit the Mixed Precipitation blog for updated information.
title: Tales of Hoffman: A Picnic Operetta

description: Local improv powerhouse Splendid Things brings their theatrical intensity, movie geekery and creepy absurdism to the BLB for a comedy display of epic proportions. They're joined each week by some of their favorite local improvisers for a cutting edge double-bill that will tilt your mind wrong… in a splendid way.
venue: Bryant Lake Bowl and Cabaret Theater
title: The Splendid Things Show

description: A ladies night for the ladies who like ladies, Booby Trap is a hot and dirty dance frenzy that features all-night performances from the Booby Trap girls, who are modern burlesque dancers/go-go girls.
title: Booby Trap

description: Deadwood: The Last Bleeping Episode is a parody of the lawless town and the filthy mouthed HBO drama (now with a pinch of comedy) it inspired. Be sure to pull on your laughing britches for a mud-slicked night of esoteric gunfighters, bartenders, prostitutes and their bleeping horses. The show even comes complete with non-vintage commercials (wonder what those are like). The show was written by award-winning funny-men Joseph Scrimshaw and Tom Poole and stars Joseph Scrimshaw as Al Swearengen. Deadwood also features Clarence Wethern, Phillip Low and Jen Scott as everyone and everything else!
venue: Bryant Lake Bowl and Cabaret Theater
title: Deadwood: The Last Bleeping Episode

description:
A gala event and retrospective presented by Eames Demetrios, Director of the Eames Foundation, who will speak on the Eames’ legacy

Demetrios’ retrospective will feature images and films from the Eames’ archives including the groundbreaking film “Powers of Ten”.
title: Charles and Ray Eames: From Furniture to the Edge of the Universe

description: “Last Laugh” is a hilarious evening of hysterical stand up comedy and outrageous improv. Featuring some of the best and brightest comedy performers on the rise, this is a night not to be missed.
venue: Bryant Lake Bowl and Cabaret Theater
title: Last Laugh

description:
The Scottsboro Boys is a thrilling musical production that is based on the notorious "Scottsboro" case in the 1930s, this case is the one in which nine African-American men were unjustly accused of a terrible crime. The show is performing at the Guthrie Theater now through September 25.

 

This daring and wildly entertaining musical explores a fascinating chapter in American history with brilliant originality. This critically-acclaimed production is directed by five-time Tony Award winner Susan Stroman (The Producers) and it is sure to steal your heart and will have you thinking deeper about our past.

 

Please know tha this proudction contains mature themes and brief nudity.
title: The Scottsboro Boys

description: The Palm Springs Art Museum will open a new exhibition featuring stunning art works created by modern masters, including Pierre Bonnard, Paul Cézanne, Marc Chagall, Edgar Degas, Roger de la Fresnaye, Alberto Giacometti, Juan Gris, Marino Marini, Henri Matisse, Henry Moore, Pablo Picasso, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Auguste Rodin, and many more significant modern artists.  The exhibition, Modern Masters Celebrate Line and Form, includes drawings, prints, sculptures and paintings drawn from the museum's permanent collection and extended loans and will be on view until September 26, 2010
title: Modern Masters Celebrate Line and Form

description:
Minnesota dance history is filled with pioneers—movers who shrugged off the expectations of their eras to make dance that matters. And the tradition continues. The SAGE Awards celebrate the mavericks among us, the dance makers who dare to be different, the artists who transform our times and embody the spirit of creative revolution. 

• Gala Event & Award Ceremony
• Live Performances by past SAGE Award Recipients
• post show reception with cash bar
• Visit www.sageawards.org for more information.
title: 6th Annual Minnesota SAGE Dance Awards

price: $12 / $10 with a Fringe button or groups of 10+
description: A hit comedy about a mismatched couple on a blind date. The audience votes on various decisions the couple needs to make, and the show takes off in wildly different directions. Stars local actors Joseph Scrimshaw, Mo Perry and Jim Robinson.
venue: Bryant Lake Bowl and Cabaret Theater
title: Adventures In Mating

description:
Named for the modest dimensions of the BLB stage, this exciting dance showcase features unfettered dance exploration. A discussion moderated by choreographer/curator Laurie Van Wieren follows each piece, giving audience and choreographer alike the opportunity to react and explore the work together.

May choreographers will be Kaleena Miller, Tim Rehborg and Julia Winkels.
venue: Bryant Lake Bowl and Cabaret Theater
title: 9x22 Dance Lab

description:
How far would you go for your child? Having kids today means that parents get to be competitive, ruthless and utterly status-conscious when it comes to giving their young the very best. There’s no room for mediocrity in a three-year olds life. Bright Idea is the story of a couple striving like hell to place their three year old in just the right preschool (PRESCHOOL!).

 Gen and Joshua Bradley are one fateful dinner party away from the ultimate success as parents: the right preschool. These parents have scrambled all of their lives to get their three-year-old son on the waiting list for the Bright Ideas Early Childhood Development Academy. You may never look at having children or preschool the same way again. This timely comedy explores the impact that our hyper-competitive culture has on the modern family.

Be warned, you may learn some new truths about yourself and those around you!
title: Bright Ideas

description: Come and sit a spell on the porch of the Mississippi Delta’s richest cotton planter as this sultry southern tale unravels family secrets. On a sweltering night, family and friends gather for Big Daddy’s birthday celebration where lies, lust, greed, and envy threaten to bubble over.
title: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof

description:
Set in a 1970's urban neighborhood barbershop, this hit musical revue mixes wisdom and song to show what love is all about. Using popular '60's and '70's R&B songs like "Can't Get Enough of Your Love," "Stop, Look, Listen," and "When a Man Loves a Woman," this play shows the world of love through the lives of four African American men. Sit back and enjoy this unforgettable show that promises to draw you into a warm embrace.

See the full show schedule here.
title: Always & Forever

description: A is for Action.. Adventure.. and Audience participation! Mr. A’s Amazing Maze Plays is a truly interactive theater experience like none other as the audience determines Suzy and her dog Neville’s course of action. The duo embarks on a precarious adventure through the mansion of suspicious Mr. Accousticus in search of the neighborhood’s stolen sounds (including Neville’s bark)! Suzy and Neville’s course of action is up to the audience in this “choose your own adventure” which offers a different telling of the story with every performance. Recommended for ages 5 and older. Due to the full-length nature of this production, children under the age of five cannot be admitted, with the exception of our Family Fun Matinee on Saturday, October 23.
title: Mr. A's Amazing Maze Plays

description: In the hustle and bustle of the holiday season, treat your family to a classic sure to inspire the spirit of the season. Revolving around Kris Kringle’s experiences at Macy’s, this is one department store stop you don’t want to miss. Mr. Kringle believes he is the real Santa Claus. Because of a disenchanting encounter with cruel cynics Mr. Kringle is spurred on to prove himself. This heartwarming tale captures hearts every time. Recommended for ages 5 and older. Due to the full-length nature of the show, children younger than five cannot be admitted, with the exception of our Family Fun Matinee on Sunday, November 28th.
title: "Miracle on 34th Street"

description: Orphaned during the Depression, these four Boxcar Children are in a fight to keep what’s left of their family together. Henry, his twin Jessie, and their younger siblings Violet and Benny, are pursued by authorities threatening to separate them into different foster homes. To complicate matters, a mysterious stranger lurks amongst them. Their distinct personalities and character strengths and flaws play a significant role in determining their fate as they discover the rewards and perils of life on the run as well as the joys of holding onto the ties that bind them together. Recommended for general audiences, including children ages five and older. Children younger than two cannot be admitted.
title: "The Boxcar Children"

description:
(Credit: Jeff Croiter)

Love is in the air and as palpable as one’s breath on a cold, clear moonless night in Almost, Maine. That love winds its way through several vignettes cloaked sometimes in the breathtaking, whimsical, humorous and even heartbreaking experiences it evokes. Just as the residents of this remote, mythical town discover, the path to love is winding and unpredictable but is-almost-always worth the journey. Recommended for mature audiences, ages 13 and older. Due to the full-length nature of the show, children younger than five cannot be admitted.
title: "Almost, Maine"

description:
(Credit: Tristram Kenton)

Proud to shine the spotlight on its own diverse mix of ever-talented artists, Lyric Arts will once again present this jubilant celebration of eclectic musical styles depicting a timeless Old Testament tale. Joseph holds a special place of honor as the first musical produced on the Main Street Stage. Just as Joseph’s coat dazzles with its vibrant array of colors, Lyric Arts celebrates 10 years of an array of dazzling memories on the Main Street Stage. Recommended for ages 5 and older. Due to the full-length nature of the show, children younger than five cannot be admitted, with the exception of our Family Fun Matinee on Saturday, February 19th.
title: "Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat"

description: An abandoned church-turned-day-spa is the setting for this hilarious southern comedy. The feisty females of Eden Falls, Georgia gather every Friday afternoon at SPA-DEE-DAH! where unexpected twists and turns challenge the women to overcome obstacles and launch their new, improved lives. This side-splitting, joyful comedy will make you laugh out loud and shout, “Hallelujah!” Recommended for ages 13 and older. Due to the full-length nature of the show, children younger than five cannot be admitted.
title: "The Hallelujah Girls"

description:
(Credit: Stephen L. Fredericks)

Lilly’s personalty is colored with more spunk and sass than Mighty Mouse and Mickey Mouse combined. Lilly loves school. She loves her pointy pencils, her glittery glasses, her shiny quarters, her friends, and of course, her teacher… Mr. Slinger. The spunky, spirited Kevin Henkes star comes to life as Lilly’s Puple Plastic Purse goes from page to stage in this Mainly for Kids presentation. Join Lilly as she learns important lessons about friendship, making mistakes, making amends, and the value of being yourself. Recommended for general audiences, including children ages five and older. Children younger than two cannot be admitted. Bring your school group to one of our School Day Matinees for only $6 per ticket! Contact the Main Street Stage Box Office for details!
title: "Lilly's Purple Plastic Purse"

description: The Brewster spinsters weave a tale of murder and mayhem that pushes the envelope in this farcical American comedy. Drama critic Mortimer Brewster simultaneously attempts to deal with his crazy family and local Brooklyn police as he debates keeping his promise to marry the woman he loves. Although the Brewster sisters are famous for their charitable acts, Mortimer discovers the homicidal duo have been murdering the lonely old men who come to their home seeking lodging with poisoned homemade wine. Just one sip of this tale will have you drowning in hijinx, intrigue, and laughter. Recommended for ages 11 and older. Due to the full-length nature of the show, children younger than five cannot be admitted.
title: "Arsenic and Old Lace"

description: Get ready to “cut loose” as Lyric Arts presents this musical stage version of this beloved 1984 foot-tapping film in which the music-loving city clicker Ren McCormack finds himself having trouble adjusting to his new life in small-town Texas. Ren is thrust into the spotlight as a debate ensues over the town’s laws prohibiting music and dancing. Set against the backdrop of a bubbly beat circa 1980′s, Ren and his classmates grapple with issues of following one’s heart, questioning society, and claiming independence. So, put on those dancin’ shoes and get ready for some footloose and fancy-free fun. Mature audiences, ages 13 and older. Due to the full-length nature of the show, children younger than five cannot be admitted.
title: "Footloose"

description: My First Time, features four actors involved in hysterical yet heartbreaking stories about their first sexual experiences—written by real people. In 1998, a website was created that allowed people to anonymously share their own true stories about their first times. The website became an instant phenomenon as over 40,000 stories poured in from around the globe that were silly, sweet, absurd, funny, heterosexual, homosexual, shy, sexy and everything in between. One of the many entries states, “File mine under clumsy and awkward”. Tickets are being sold now via Ticketmaster, so get your tickets now and enjoy one of the best plays of the summer!
title: My First Time

description:
The dramatic production of tenderness, charm and beauty written by Tennessee Williams is playing at the Jungle Theater now through October 17.

The Glass Menagerie is set in a rundown apartment in a St. Louis ghetto, all while Southern belle Amanda Wingfield, her painfully shy daughter, Laura and her aspiring poet son, Tom, form a triangle of quiet desperation.  Amanda, an overbearing single mother, lives on memories of her flower-scented youth, while her children bear the weight of her unrealistic dreams for their future.  But when a gentleman caller offers false hope to the family, their precarious world shatters with haunting results.
title: The Glass Menagerie

description:
Adapted for the stage by Pulitzer Prize-winning dramatist Marsha Norman from the best-selling novel by Louise Erdrich, The Master Butchers Singing Club chronicles the intersecting lives of German immigrant and butcher Fidelis and sideshow performer Delphine as they settle into the small town of Argus, North Dakota. This famed play will be in production at the Guthrie through November 6.

The story is bookended by the two World Wars and set against a tapestry of song, this moving story traces the bond between a mother and her child, the boundless friendship between two women and one’s life-changing discovery of true love.

Visit the Guthrie's website for ticket information and pricing.
title: The Master Butchers Singing Club

description: Life, death, and the mind are the subjects of “Dreams”, a new play by Christopher Wall. The show unfolds at its own easy (almost lazy) pace, recounting a troubled pair of romances between two single parents and their adolescent offspring in a nowheresville town. The set—weeds sprouting among washing machines, designed by David Newell—fulfills the title's potential for surrealism. But what's truly impressive about this show is how, slowly and oddly, it reveals itself to be a memory play split among four perspectives. Director Giovanna Sardelli establishes a quiet, contemplative tone, although she doesn't balance that with momentum or focus. That's up to the lead, Stevie Ray Dallimore, who fortunately gives his role of everyman teen a charming vulnerability. But mostly, this is Wall's show. He's got a canny approach to structure, a knack for dramatic metaphor, and most importantly, emotional honesty that lends "Dreams" a satisfying weight.
title: Dreams of the Washer King

description: The landmark musical returns to Broadway. Do I need to tell you what it's about? (“Romeo and Juliet” in the barrio.) Or how beautiful the music is? (Very.) Or how cute the stars look? (As puppies.) No, I'll just mention that “America!” sounds even better in Spanish. That's the only update for the 21st century – why mess with what works?
title: West Side Story

description: This melancholy rock musical is ready for Broadway after prep runs in DC and Off-Broadway. Despite its use of rock music, its themes sound more like Sondheim – an ordinary group of folks, here a suburban family – while Alice Ripley's turn as a bipolar mother is already getting Tony buzz.
title: Next to Normal

description: This musical thrilled audiences Off-Broadway last season, and it's not hard to see why. Fela Kuti was a guru of Afrobeat, a 1970s fusion of jazz, funk, chant, and polyrhythm—but he was also an outspoken supporter of African rights, social justice, and economic equality. The combo of music and politics is an explosive combo!
title: Fela!

description: We'd think a star of Catherine Zeta-Jones's wattage would be shining all over Times Square, but we've seen nary an ad for her New York stage debut. She plays opposite Broadway's beloved Angela Lansbury in this sophisticated romance. Don't get turned off by the subject matter (a summer weekend of simmering liaisons in Sweden): Sondheim's "Night Music" is one of the best musicals in Broadway's songbook.
title: A Little Night Music

description:
The Harrison Center (Credit: Submitted photo)

Like most great summer plans, this show came together at the last minute. The basement of the Harrison Center will feature incisive new work by four emerging artists — Jeff Geesa, Audra McClelland, Jenny Ollikainen and Diego Yanto — all with unconventional takes on this nation of ours. Out front, enjoy a barbecue with sparklers, sprinklers and acoustic music by The No-Ops.
title: Stars and Stripes or Whatever Artist Reception

description:
"Night Watch" by Kate Oberreich (Credit: Submitted photo)

Rice paper, doilies, tissues, fabrics and colored pencils — they all find their way into graphically abstract landscape works by 29-year-old artist Kate Oberreich. Upwards of 15 layers are fused together, with even more layers of acrylic paint. “I’ll do something, hate it and then have to cover it up with something,” she says. “I never throw a canvas away because you can always sandwich more stuff on it. And, it adds to the character of the final piece.”

Details: Shows from March 18 through March 27, Wug Laku’s Studio & Garage, 1125 Brookside Ave., Suite C7 (inside the Circle City Industrial Complex), free, (317) 270-8258 or www.wlsandg.com.
title: The layered effect

description: Dum duh-duh dum <snap snap> In this musical version of the Great American Family, Nathan Lane ("The Producers") and Bebe Neuwirth ("Cheers", "Chicago") star as Gomez and Morticia Addams, the delightfully dark heads of the famous family. The creators have gone back to the original cartoons for their inspiration. Should be fiendish fun!
title: The Addams Family

description: Twenty-five Downtown art galleries open for viewing. Presented by the Indianapolis Downtown Artists & Dealers Association.
title: IDADA First Friday

description:
The Wooster Group are pioneers of American theater. Even this revival of a Reagan-era work is far ahead of most plays that people consider experimental―and yet it's also accessible to the most inexperienced theatergoer. In fact, it's almost a soap opera, following budding romance on an American warship late in the Cold War. Frances McDormand and Maura Tierney (“ER”) join the Group's ensemble for this piece.

A Metromix Theater Pick of the Week

Review
The title inverts “South Pacific”, a clue to what the Wooster Group's doing here. The show's an ultra-hip parody of classic WW2 romances about horndog sailors and frisky nurses. But it's filtered through the Wooster sensibility: an almost robotic style of production that extends to the too-loud country-song interludes. Still, it's their most accessible show, with a linear plot and everything. The Group tickles the American habit of conflating military strength and hetero sex, but they also hit a dark undercurrent of violence (including a waterboarding scene) and sexual exploitation. The script's packed with oddball lines, as quotable as a Coen Brothers movie. And the cast excels: Wooster regular Ari Fliakos has the smug grin and smooth gab of a Billy Wilder rake, while Maura Tierney (in a killer GI Jane haircut) surprises by shifting smoothly from “ER” melodrama to avant-garde theater. This heady, dizzying, must-see drama.

A Hand In The Inadvertent" will feature works by artist Hugh Leeman. Hugh Leeman's current works recount a year of experimentation with mediums that all share a hand in the inadvertent. In this body of work Hugh has employed the use of blowtorches and candles to "draw" with as well as chemical reactions through which he "paints." Additionally, he uses tar to accent his works and oil paint to incorporate his signature realistic portraiture. All of these works gain a creative independence from his previous bodies of work as they are experimental and and, at times, documentative of the artistic process reacting to an inadvertent condition set in motion by his use of non-traditional media. These works hold principle to Hugh's previous career works by remaining strongly influenced by the urban environment. His subjects are transient street musicians, rolling stones, and strangers all given a due through a moment to tell a bit of their story as translated by the artist's hands. Hugh Leeman is a self-taught, San Francisco based artist. His gallery work has been exhibited in New York, San Francisco and at The Museum of Mexico City. He is recognized for his gallery portraiture which captures in raw emotion the lives of his subjects whom he meets on the inner city streets. Though best known for his street art, which has adorned walls from Varanasi, India to Indiana and from New York, London, and the divided Palestinian Territories to Bogota, Colombia. Most recently Leeman created the first ever MLK, Jr. mural overlooking his historic birth house. His subjects, often marginalized by society, are recast into potentially heroic roles before being pasted all over the world. His street art has additionally evolved into the "t-shirt project" in which he gives back to his subjects by printing his art onto shirts which they sell and keep 100% of the profits from. (August 2010) - Hugh Leeman's Martin Luther King, Jr. mural in Atlanta, Georgia brought national press attention. In Hugh's own words, he shares the following experience: Atlanta, GA "This mural sits a block between the Martin Luther King, Jr. historical society and Dr. King's birth house, overlooking the heart of the MLK, Jr. district of Atlanta. Initially I was given permission to do this mural by the restaurant owners of The Sound Table, who lease this building. Just before my arrival in Atlanta from San Francisco I found this permission had been revoked by the buildings owner who was vacationing in Alaska. He both permits and profits from this Old English Ad on his building. The Ad agency in no way would allow any infringement on its space on this wall even an MLK mural on his own doorstep. My plane had arrived in Atlanta much later than expected due to an emergency landing in Wichita, Kansas. Finally in Atlanta I dropped my bags and walked at 1a.m. to the restaurant, calling its owners on the way. Wanting to hear why my permission had been revoked in person, I received an interesting twist of fate as one of the owners had gone to R.I.S.D. with Sheperd Fairey and could appreciate this murals value. The Sound Tables open mind and ability to see away an injustice served by the hands of corporate advertising are what initially and finally made this mural possible. In between a property owner, and ad agency, and an ad so distastefully placed in this historic district had blocked our permission. Word spread fast through the neighborhood that scaffolding and a giant MLK mural was going up. As art holds the beautiful potential to interpretation we began hearing "this is great but why is it next to an "Old E" advertisement - that's not cool." So initially blocked by Old E then forced to downsize the mural by more than half only to have the mural interpreted as slander towards him and all he represents. We saw this as a beautiful opportunity to start a dialogue amongst all those who saw this mural and ad next to one another. Two signs were posted between the mural and the Ad. The one pointing to the Ad "The Sound Table and muralist Hugh Leeman neither endorse, condone, nor benefit from this advertisement." And another pointing to the new MLK mural stating "The Sound Table would like to thank Hugh Leeman and the Living Walls crew for this beautiful and uplifting addition to the Old 4th Ward." Finally after countless hours painting, printing, cutting, drawing upon 20 feet of scaffolding, and what seemed like endless amounts of 97 degree Atlanta summer sweat we had started to set the record straight. Only two hours after finishing I am on my way to the airport and get a text from The Sound Table, "The Ad Agency has sent a crew to paint over their ad and the signs we posted." minutes later " They say it had nothing to do with the mural only a coincidence." This is beautiful to see the Old English Ad go away and an MLK mural overlook his birth house. And should another ad go up to take this ones place hopefully it is in better taste to this honorable area. A special thanks to The Sound Table for giving me your wall and Living Walls for giving me great assistants and steady scaffolding. " -Hugh Leeman From press release

Located in the Historic Boyce Block 224 East Main Street Muncie, IN 47305 ph. 765.284.8422 genny@gordyframing.com www.gordyframing.com www.TurtlePaintings.com - Watercolors of Indiana & Maine Exhibit by Local Artist Retired Ball State Architecture Professor, author of books on the art of sketching, avid traveler and artist of watercolors, Paul Laseau has a knack for capturing time in his works of art. A moment on a French boulevard or a century in a Greek village, Laseau paintings, sketches and photos all boast a crispness that would have viewers believe the creation was effortless. But just try to copy the confident lines, washes and finished scenes; it becomes clear that these are the works of a very seasoned hand following a similarly seasoned eye. Upon questioning his motivation for the subject matter of this exhibit, the prolific artist gave a rather archeological view. "It represents my continuing fascination with the interaction of people and nature through the evidence found in landscapes." Offers gallery owner, Brian Gordy, "In this exhibit, the artist, as historian, shows us our own world." Landscapes by Paul Laseau is the September exhibit at Gordy Fine Art & Framing Company in Muncie. Laseau, a featured artist of the downtown gallery, will greet patrons and guests at an opening reception on September 2nd from 5 to 8 PM where he will discuss his work and answer questions. Light refreshments will be served and the public is invited to attend. Twenty to twenty five paintings featuring majestic barns, Indiana countryside, and the Maine coast will hang throughout the month and may also be viewed during normal business hours, or by appointment. For more information, contact the gallery at 765-284-8422 or visit http://www.gordyframing.com . Gordy Fine Art & Framing is located in the historic Boyce Block at 224 East Main Street in downtown Muncie. From press release

description: Indianapolis - Provocative images of the World Trade Center will be on display at Chase Towers at 111 Monument Circle in downtown Indianapolis beginning September through the end of the month. The images, taken by photographer Slawek before the events of Sept. 11, 2001, depict a cemetery with the trade center's twin towers as a back drop. Slawek's title for the exhibit is REFLECTIONS: Manhattan Rhapsody, Part 1. The photographs will be displayed along with a collection of other Slawek works. The photographs were taken while the artist was commuting from Long Island to Manhattan in the mid 1990s. Concerning his collection the artist says, "From the car, I admired the fascinating urban landscapes. By unifying the headstones of an old European cemetery in Queens with the beautiful Manhattan skyscrapers in the distance, the photos depict the old world with the world I view today". Slawek travels around the world and his work often captures reflected images. Born in communist Poland, he moved to the United States in the 1980s and his path has taken him from the Manhattan to the Midwest, where he resides in Indianapolis. This is the third time Slawek has been invited to display his works at the Chase Tower, which is a popular space for Indiana artists to display photography and paintings. Noted Slawek of his work, "It is the result of my fascination with the beauty of life's forms from yesterday and today. My hope is to not offend, but rather to inspire new ways of thinking and viewing the world for those who are able to see this collection," said Slawek. From press relese

Their latest piece plants its feet on the Lower East Side of two eras: the 1890s wave of immigrants and the 1990s wave of lost artists. A pair of actors play couples from both eras.
title: Now Circa Then

description: Photography by Freddi Stevens-Jacobi from travel photos to artistic statements exploring the diversity of "window treatments" and what those views reveal about our daily landscapes. In the ArtSpace.
title: Window Treatment: Looking Out and Looking In

description: After almost a full year as Stutz Residents, two of the city's most talented, emerging artists say their work has evolved and expanded as a result of the experience. The public will have the opportunity to see the results of this growth during the month of September, when the artists' works are featured in an exhibition. Awarded free studio space and utilities in the Stutz Building for one year, 2009-2010 Stutz Residents Burris and Flaherty both describe their time a period of expansion. Having more space dedicated to creating art allowed them to pursue new ideas and improve themselves as artists, they said. A painter who mixes fantastic, colorful images with earthy and dark tones, Lydia Burris creates pictures that would seem at home in dreams or nightmares. Like the roots that form faces beneath green shoots in her paintings, bits of mystery and whimsy lie beneath the surface of each work, entertaining and intriguing viewers. At the Stutz, she said, she felt encouraged to paint more, experimenting with different styles and pushing her creativity to new levels. Patrick Flaherty found himself focusing primarily on one series of paintings in his year of Stutz Residency. A body of work that has been evolving for about five years, his Analog Series revolves around anthropomorphized television sets placed in bizarre landscapes and situations. At the Stutz, he said, he delved more deeply into this series, expanding the subject matter and sharpening the stories the paintings tell. From press release
title: Exploration: 2009-10 Stutz Residents Lydia Burns and Patrick Flaherty
Fela!

description: Edie Falco (“The Sopranos”) and Alison Pill (“Mauritius”) face off in this two-hander about second chances and ex-cons. The playwright's Chloe Moss, who wrote one of our favorite shows of last spring (“Christmas is Miles Away”) and the director's Anne Kauffman (“Stunning”); all four women are dynamos of creativity, making this an essential show for the spring season!
title: This Wide Night

description: Works by mosaic artist.
title: Michele Soncini

description: Autumn vistas from Indiana through the mountains of the Eastern United States to the Coast of Maine by nature artist Jim Salem and works by international photographer Alexey Stiop. Ongoing exhibits also feature: Terri McClatchie's earth art; Stacia Alexander's portraits and landscapes and contemporary artist Megan Hart.
title: Landscapes and Beyond

description: Edie Falco (“The Sopranos”) and Alison Pill (“Milk”) face off in this two-hander about second chances and ex-cons. The playwright's Chloe Moss, who wrote one of our favorite shows of last spring (“Christmas is Miles Away”) and the director's Anne Kauffman; all four women are dynamos of creativity, making this an essential show for the spring season!
title: This Wild Night

description: Oil painter Heidi Harner and photographer Freddie Kelvin present stories of spirit and tranquility in their portraits of breeze-blown horses and contemplative landscapes. Original works by two dozen award-winning Indiana artists on view.
title: Visions of Nature

description: Contemporary and traditional painting by Gretchen Ten Eyck Hunt. In the gallery.
title: Exploring the Power of Color

description: This cutting-edge drama wrestles with the ethical implications of 21st-century science. A student who's more interested in liquor than lab-work proposes a thesis that exposes the fundamental assumptions of biotech research. The show's cowritten by a playwright and a scientist, so expect surprises in concept and execution!
title: Sweet Sweet Motherhood

description: Watercolor, oil and acrylic paintings are scenes from the artist's travels through the U.S. and abroad.
title: Betty Boyle Exhibit

description: A Christmas pageant in Lincoln's hometown sets off a controversy when someone implies that our 16th President might have enjoyed the company of men! To add to the fun, each act tells the same events from a different point-of-view. “ALBGDP” was the toast of the last year's Fringe Festival & sounds like a blast!
title: Abraham Lincoln's Big Gay Dance Party

description: Artists, community members and schools make small-scale memorials out of wine boxes in honor of loved ones.
title: Shrine Exhibition

description: Works by artists working in 3-D media. Artists: Thomas Ramey, Max Stolkin, Matt Berg, James Wille Faust, Robert Pulley, Jaci Willis, Brad Howe and others.
title: Forms of Process, Fall Sculpture

description:
The newest play by Edward Albee ("Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?") sees the grand master in familiar territory: identity and family. A mother can't tell her identical twins apart, especially since one claims that the other doesn't exist! Co-starring Brian Murray, a great interpreter of Albee's sinister men, and theatrical grand dame Elizabeth Ashley.

A Metromix Theater Pick of the Week
title: Me, Myself and I

description: Abstract color, train yards, and movie stars will take center stage, or center-wall rather, at the Evan Lurie Gallery on September 18, 2010 when the space opens its first show of the fall entitled "Crossing Paths" featuring Adam Normandin, Daniela Wicki and Ben Freeman. Ben Freeman returns to the Evan Lurie Gallery with a new collection of work, which, although technically in line with his delicate style of work atop antiqued paperwork, will this time include glamorous male icons of the silver screen in addition to the lovely starlets of yesteryear. Leading men such as Humphrey Bogart, Marlon Brando and Clark Gable will share the show's limelight with easily recognizable Judy Garland among other prominent women of Hollywood. Borrowing a bit from his education in architectural structure and fusing it with his education in Fine Arts from North Carolina University, Freeman's style is as unmistakable as it is engrossing. The artist paints his figures and faces on a expansive bed of archival media including old postcards, letters and photos that serve the pieces well adding not just depth of imagination but also a forgone connection left to the interpretation of the viewer. Joining the exhibit and debuting in the gallery for his first show is Adam Normandin - an artist who finds beauty in the details of the unobserved. A graduate of Hofstra University, Normandin's work is exhibited across the United States and held in many prominent collections. With a body of recent work that focuses on the locomotive industry, Normandin's fascination with the freight train is readily observed and memorizing as it pushes the boundary of the traditional. Leaving little behind, Normandin captures his subjects without prejudice incorporating rust spots, graffiti markings and imperfections in place as he redefines the scene in a somewhat cropped characterization. Of his work he states, "I rarely choose my subjects, instead they draw me to them Years of use and exposure to the elements imprint a sense of tireless duty onto these objects." Also with her first appearance on the walls at 30 West Main Street will be Daniela Wicki whose work in the abstract takes on a very distinct energetic tone. With a style that has been hailed as "exciting and vibrant", Wicki finds her inspiration in the development of each piece and the work required to see the process through to completion. Once a successful lawyer in New York, this daughter of Swiss parents born in Lima, Peru has traveled a path from classic training of technique during her teenage years through to her style of abstract vision in a lifelong passion for creative expression. "For me, art is an aesthetic, ethical and ultimately spiritual force: a challenge made in the experience of finding in each and every creation a self realization, a self portrait of my own energy, a landscape of forces, life in motion rather than still-life." From press release
title: Crossing Paths

description: Broadway hosts a revival of this classic drama about the oldest profession. Kitty Warren explains to her daughter how hard times and limited opportunities led her to become a successful entrepreneur. Emmy-winner Cherry Jones (“24”) stars in the title role; in 1995, she won a Tony and made her rep in another Shaw comedy.
title: Mrs. Warren's Profession

description: Retrospective of early works from artist's collection, including paintings from graduate school (circa 1955) as well as new paintings available in the gallery.
title: Kellar Mahaney Revisited

description:
Metromix review
<!-- @page { margin: 0.79in } P { margin-bottNo playwright feels more current than Sheila Callaghan. In her latest New York show, a modern artist collects roadkill for her installations, hoping to harness a fatal virus out of a Bruckheimer flick. The ultra-cool provocateur plays a cat-and-mouse game with a private security-consultant who's got Nick Fury's eyepatch and Capt. Kirk's delivery. The show piles up the ideas to investigate the role of artists in the Age of Terrorism. But despite the heady themes, cool tone, and theatrical use of high-tech surveillance equipment, “Roadkill” isn't just arid intellectualism. Callaghan has a sick sense of wit (enter the artist covered in gore: “Excuse the mess, I was flossing…”) and a sly fondness for big action movie plots. The production has its problems though. Kip Fagan's ultra-cool style undercuts the domestic thriller plot and squelches the satire. And in the lead roles, Rebecca Henderson Danny Mastrogiorgio don't share much chemistry. Still, the hip theatergoer shouldn't miss this cool work.
title: Roadkill Confidential

description: "Up and down" art.
title: Sofiya Inger: Short Flights of This Summer

description: The Broadway transfer of Kneehigh's richly rewarding drama about a doomed love affair in pre-war England. The repressed emotions find a counterpart in the inventive staging: a cinema-stage hybrid with script by Noel Coward “Private Lives”) and filmed by David Lean ("Bridge on the River Kwai").
title: Brief Encounter

description: Regional, juried show that explores the use of urban and rural landscape in contemporary art. The exhibition, which showcases the varied stylistic and conceptual approaches the artists have toward landscape, features painting, drawing, printmaking, ceramics, sculpture, and mixed-media pieces by artists from Indiana, Ohio, Michigan, Illinois, and Kentucky. Presented by INvision.
title: Seeing the Land

description: Lillian Hellman's iconic proto-feminist drama gets rejuvenated by Dutch director Ivo van Hove and his NYC muse, Elizabeth Marvel. Set in the South, a clan of wives must negotiate for their rights in the face of stubborn men and family tradition. Reportedly, van Hove adds a racial element as well.
title: The Little Foxes

description: Exhibit for Potters Council. Featured artists: Melisa Cadell, Fong Choo, Molly Hatch, Kathy King and Tom Meuninck.
title: Splendid Surfaces

description: Off-Broadway's most anticipated show of the season. The Signature Theater revives Tony Kushner's two-part masterpiece about AIDS, Mormons, anti-Communism, and angels. Zachary Quinto (“Star Trek”, “Heroes”) leads the talented cast. If you only see one play this fall, & you can find a ticket, see “Angels in America”.
title: Angels in America
Gallery 924 Opening Reception Featuring the Art of Ben Johnson

description: The hermit-like life of an aging woman is interrupted by a feral suitor and a visitor from her past. A Gothic romance with a 21st-century tone, this inventive new drama takes a unique approach to language and stage imagery―which you should always expect from the cutting-edge Soho Rep.
title: Orange Hat and Grace
Early Indiana, American, European and Russian Impressionism

description: A classic musical to give Tea Partiers fits: unemployed workers unionize against wealthy plutocrats and political tools. This 1930s Broadway hit is as relevant today as it was in the Great Depression. “Cradle” is offered in a barebones format―a piano and no set―that stays true to the show's politics.
title: The Cradle Will Rock
Holiday One Piece Show

description: In "New Play," the ensemble cast writes a new play while performing, thereby debuting (and closing) a new work every week.
title: New Play

description: You remember Zero Mostel—he was in “The Producers” with Gene Wilder. Well, this one-man biodrama reveals the fascinating history of a man who suffered under the infamous Hollywood Blacklist, made a comeback in the original “Fiddler on the Rood” and most notably, charmed everyone with an oversize personality.
title: Zero Hour

description: Two strangers find their lives tangled together after a one-night stand. This drama about sex and abortion, set in the titular city, has been feted at the prestigious Humana Festival earlier in the month. The Barrow Group lets you see what the hubbub's about.
title: Phoenix

description: In WW2, a naked man with amnesia washes up on a small island in the English Channel. Is he a Nazi or a Limey, a spy or a madman? A potent piece of mystery about identity and war by one of England's top playwrights, Moira Buffini.
title: Gabriel

description: It's hard to be enthusiastic about a new play by AR Gurney, a stolid craftsman who's been cranking plays out since the 1960s. His latest, a nostalgic ode to post-war Broadway, sounds artistically and culturally conservative but its skilled cast of middle-aged performers give it a veneer of quality.
title: The Grand Manner

description: Before Rosa Parks ignited the Civil Rights movement, Sgt. Isaac Woodard found himself a tragic hero. Beaten, blinded, and arrested by Southern police (while still in uniform, no less!), Woodard's case became a national cause and led directly to the integration of the Armed Forces. This biodrama tells his story.
title: Reflections of a Heart

description: A backstage drama from Primary Stages. A young actor with stars in his eyes befriends his idol in the hopes that networking will open doors―but their complicated relationship causes him to question his principles and his dreams of stardom. The production transfers from California, where it won numerous awards.
title: Secrets of the Trade

description: Talk about Off-Broadway: this show is staged in an anonymous living room somewhere in Manhattan. There's another catch: the address is secret! It's an intimate staging and a flashy way to draw attention to yet another production of Ibsen's masterpiece. If you can get a reservation, you'll be told where to go. If not, you'll never know.
title: Hedda Gabler

description: A revival of the Amoralist's kitchen-sink melodrama. A palooka from Coney Island keeps one eye on a martial arts championship belt and the other on his hot-to-trot wife. Bursting with paperclip twists and contrived subplots, “Happy” is real downtown theater, held together by love, energy, and credit card debt. And every time Sarah Lemp strides onstage, the show turns from kitsch fun into theater art.
title: Happy in the Poorhouse

description: Edwin Booth was most famous American actor of the 1850s; his brother, John Wilkes Booth, was pretty good too. This historical drama looks at their sibling rivalry, a professional and romantic jealousy that may have caused the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.
title: An Error of the Moon

description:
Metromix Review
There are two stories in Lucy Thurber's over-earnest play, but only one of them's a drama. The other is a novel-within-a-play that helps the grieving process of show's young heroine. As she reads her late sister's novel, cool New Yorker Abigail deals with the collapse of a surrogate family and with a lover who's too happy to avoid emotional intimacy. But novels generally aren't dramatic (otherwise they'd be dramas), partly because the most important activity tends to occur in the mind. As amiable as Thurber's farmhand romance of a novel is, it belongs on a page, not in a theater. The framing story suits the stage more, even though it's also introspective—it's got events and tension. But a play this introverted needs a cast that's confident about the dialogue's subtext, and here director Caitriona McLaughlin fails them. A stronger production might show “World” to be impressionistic and evocative, but probably not as deep as it hopes to be.
title: Bottom of the World

description: A new drama set out west, where jobs are tough to find and so's forgiveness. A disgraced Evangelical hopes to reunite with his estranged son and prays for the Second Coming (whichever comes first). This three-hander is presented by Partial Comfort, a scrappy young troupe.
title: A Bright New Boise

description: Sarah Ruhl, possibly the most influential new American playwright of the last decade, adapts the classic novel by Virginia Woolf. Ruhl's poetic, intimate voice and deep sense of compassion should complement Woolf well. The novel follows a young man in Queen Elizabeth's court who (a) lives forever, and (b) magically turns into a woman.
title: Orlando

description: The most popular and best-acclaimed shows from August's Fringe Festival get remounted, in case you missed them. Check out our summary of the Fest here. We particularly liked “The Twentieth-Century Way”; we're glad to have a second chance to catch “Getting Even with Shakespeare”. What about you?
title: FringeNYC Encores 2010

description:
Metromix Review
“The Revival” vividly evokes the atmosphere of Hot Springs, AK, building up the Baptist worldview through a hundred folksy touches, like the pastor checking the Monday paper for its ranking of church attendance. The set, by Kevin Judge, suggests the individualist, go-for-the-gut approach of modern Baptism by drawing your focus to an imposing, rough-hewn cross: this God loves but He also damns. We can feel the underground heat that warms the town's springs. But elsewhere, the show offers a pat, predictable drama of a Man in Doubt. This paper-checking pastor can't inspire his flock and only feels himself when he sneaks off to his lover, a meth-brewing JD. Though his sins tear at his psyche, they're the stuff of so much theater it's impossible to feel invested in his salvation. A genuine moral quandary or a sense of complicity to match the protagonist's moral confusion would help move us more than this shaggy dog of a play.
title: The Revival

description: A one-man show by Daniel Beaty, whose superb talents earned him an Obie for “Emergence-See” a few years ago. He provides the words and actions for six black men, ages 10 to 60 as they live through one transformative night. Beaty's warmth and humanity add depth to a virtuoso chameleonic performance.
title: Through the Night

description: A grad student manages the tricky transition from her jobless paralysis to an equally frustrating workplace. Sam Gold (“Circle Mirror Transformation”) has snagged a quartet of talented actors for this comedy that will cut close to the bone for twentysomething ticket-holders.
title: Tigers Be Still

description: A drama about environmental activism that practices what it preaches. “Capsule 33” is powered entirely by sustainable energy (including a bike that you can pedal to add energy to the performance!). The subject is the only man living in Nakagin Capsule Tower, a green apartment building in Tokyo.
title: Capsule 33

description: A campus drama set in the 1970s, written specifically by AR Gurney (“The Dining Room”) for the Bats, a resident company of talented young actors. This world premiere runs headlong into the Canon Wars, when young minority and female students dared to ask their profs why all the classics were written by dead white men.
title: Office Hours

description: From the writer of “Billy Elliot”, Lee Hall, comes this true story of proletarian heroism and artistic expression. A group of English miners dabbling in oil-painting become acclaimed for their technique and vision. “Pitman” is a British import, arriving from its sold-out run at the London's National Theatre.
title: The Pitman Painters

description: Transferring to Broadway after its popular autumn run, “Irena's Vow” offers the sort of inspirational plot that actors love. Tovah Feldshuh plays a Polish housekeeper who hides a dozen Jews from the Nazi death squads led by her boss. It's noble and undeniably important, but also a little schmaltzy and safe.
title: Irena's Vow

description: Aquila, an underrated crew of Brits and Americans, have been refining their adaptation of Homer's epic for a decade. Inspired by images of D-Day, this imaginative staging is a visceral delight for fans of physical acting and classical myth.
title: Illiad: Book One

description: The Flying Karamazov Brothers, world-famous jugglers, return to Gotham for an open-ended run. If you've never caught their astonishing, delightful act, you're in for a treat! Vulgar comedy and breathtaking artistry make a great combination, and like most real, old-fashioned entertainment, it benefits immensely from being seen live.
title: 4Play

description: A biodrama about the crossed romance between two of Hollywood's biggest stars, European emigrés Marlene Dietrich and Maurice Chevalier. The dramatic hook is that Chevalier was stuck entertaining Nazis in Occupied France while Dietrich was playing to GIs on the USO circuit.
title: Dietrich and Chevalier: The Musical

description: Another worth-yet-forgotten play from the Mint Theater. This one, by a woman playwright (a rarity before the 1970s), is set in Ireland, where young James Whelan may have married more women than he can manage, and certainly more than can make him happy. Forgotten since 1956, this is its New York premiere!
title: Wife to James Whelan

description:
The core of “Power Balladz” is a comic romance about an '80s hair-metal rocker who gets a second chance to win the heart of his high school sweetie. It's got live trivia and live-band karaoke, a fog machine, long feathered male hair-dos, and songs by Guns 'N' Roses, Journey, Heart, Queens, Bon Jovi, Styx and others.

A Metromix Theater Pick of the Week!
title: Power Balladz

description: A nebbishy comedy about a washed-up TV writer and his one last shot at show biz. Coincidentally, playwright Kenny Solms used to be a TV comedy writer in the 1970s. The show stars Peter Scolari (the Bosom Buddy who wasn't Tom Hanks) and a grabbag of jobbing Off-Broadway actors.
title: It Must Be Him

description: Shaw’s classic about a smart young woman who learns that her mother (Cherry Jones) runs a set of brothels
title: Mrs. Warren’s Profession

description: Tony-winners Patti LuPone & Brian Stokes Mitchell star in this musical adaptation of Pedro Almadovar’s film
title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown

description: Shows at the Rattlestick tend to extremes: either superb or dull. Hard to tell which this will be. Actor-turned-playwright Florencia Lozano takes audiences into a Hispanic home where the effects of foreign wars and domestic chaos inspire fear and terror.
title: UnderneathMyBed

description: A shocking monologue that lets audiences into the mind of a serial killer. Is he a scourge of God or simply a psychopath? Can we understand a mass murderer on his own terms—and should we try? Part of the city-wide 2010 Irish Festival, and a success at the '08 Edinburgh Fringe Fest.
title: Absolution

description: An Irishman is surprised to see that his twin brother's girlfriend has a doppelganger zooming around Dublin. A tight, noirish little drama about love, vengeance, and sibling rivalry from a DC troupe devoted to the work of the Emerald Isle. Part of the city-wide 2010 Irish Festival.
title: The Prophet of Monto

description: Two plays in one, set in the same apartment in two eras. In the past, young newlyweds discover the trials of married life; in the present, retired spouses navigate the lapsed intimacies of their own marriage. Part of the city-wide 2010 Irish Festival, this show premiered in Dublin.
title: Exit/Entrance

description: Charles Busch is a master of Off-Broadway's campy genre parody. His latest gives the burlesque treatment to movies set in nunneries—think TCM classics like “The Bells of St. Mary's” or “The Song of Bernadette”. Busch plays Mother Superior to a postulant with 'visions', an outbreak of sexual hysteria, and the return of an old suitor.
title: The Divine Sister

description: For some reason, we love plays that feature librarians. This 1975 drama by Michael Frayn (“Noises Off”, “Copenhagen”) sees Lucy, a scatterbrain who runs the archives of a smalltown newspaper, challenged by a young woman with a zeal for order. A 'sincere' comic drama from the Keen Company.
title: Alphabetical Order

description: A tongue-in-cheek docudrama about the making of an infamous 1970s porno that broke American taboos (and laws) against oral sex. Follow Linda Lovelace and company from the filming to the raids and arrests to the courtrooms and on into history & Wikipedia. Naturally, the show contains adult themes & nudity.
title: The Deep Throat Sex Scandal

description: Who's fit to be a parent? Two gay men are ready to become fathers, while the mother of one man, a recent widow, wants their help to restart her own family. Wrestling with queer issues, immigration, and race, “A Home Across the Ocean” was selected as part of the '10 National Newborn Festival.
title: A Home Across the Ocean

description: Fans of Chekhovian drama shouldn't miss this collection of one-acts and short stories adapted for the stage by Michael Frayn (“Copenhagen”). But it should also provide the curious with a good introduction to the unique, subtle style of that master of book and stage. Includes versions of “The Bear” and “The Evils of Tobacco”.
title: The Sneeze

description: The Quantum Eye is professional magician Sam Eaton's  exploration of mentalism, magic, perception and deception. It's currently the longest-running one-man Off-Broadway magic show in New York.
title: The Quantum Eye

description: Via the organizers: Beginning in September, The Tank and Full Circle Theatre Company are producing a monthly staged reading series featuring plays in the public domain with no copyright restrictions. Once a play has entered public domain, it belongs to everyone. It becomes ours to do with as we please. As such, we thought it'd be cool if we offered up some of the creative decision-making to our audiences. We've selected our first seven plays, and seven directors with very different approaches. We had our audiences assign a play to each director. Polls closed on July 6th and the results are in! What do you get when you mix treachery, morality, wounds that won't heal, Heracles's bow and arrows, a chorus of sailors, and the fate of the Trojan War? The answer: a legend that three of the most celebrated Greek playwrights wrote about. After contracting an obnoxiously smelly snakebite on the way to Troy, Philoctetes finds himself aban
title: Public Domain: Garrett Zuercher directs 'Philoctetes' by Sophocles

description: When second-rate chorus girl and would-be star Roxie Hart goes on trial for murder, she makes the system work for her, parlaying the abundant media attention into fortune and fame. Set in 1927, the show's themes have retained their relevance.
title: Chicago

description: When sorority darling Elle Woods' boyfriend dumps her because he's looking for someone more serious, Elle goes where no Delta Nu has ever ventured: Haravard Law.
title: Legally Blonde

description: Via the organizers: A painless way to meet Casting Directors and more...! Every Tuesday night, StageBuddy.com hosts an Actors Event/Talk show in the West Village. Upcoming Casting Directors over the next few weeks include: Stephanie Klapper, Scott Wojcik, Michael Cassara, Dani Super, Duncan Stewart, Ken Lazer and more. There are also Producers, Directors, Filmmakers and many more people with casting abilities for you to meet and greet and listen to their stories and advice. The cost? Only $5... it's well worth it. At 6:30pm is a networking party and at 7pm is the talk show. More info at: http://www.stagebuddy.com/live
title: StageBuddy's Showbiz Talk

description: Via the organizers: Part of 1st Irish Theatre Festival, Belinda McKeon’s “Graham & Frost” is the eviscerating drama of three men from very different walks of life, who set about reopening an abandoned restaurant in the old Italian section of Williamsburg. Each has a stake in the old place, and each has something from which they want to hide. Behind the dusty storefront's still-shuttered door, they will not allow one another to escape as they are forced to face the secrets and the fears that stalk them all.
title: Graham & Frost

description:
From the organizers:

As of Thursday, May 27 Joe Marshall’s A Night In Vegas has found a new home at The Bleecker Street Theatre (45 Bleecker Street). Directed by Joe Marshall, opening bight will be Saturday, June 5. Premium seats are $50 and general admission tickets are $35 and can be purchased by visiting Telecharge.com. (Please Note: A Night In Vegas has a special preview performance schedule listed below and beginning June 10 will play Thursday – Saturday at 10:30PM). Set in the gayest hotel on the Vegas strip, Joe Marshall’s award-winning comedy A Night in Vegas is a raucous comedy that features six vignettes that covers everything from male prostitutes to anonymous sex, to gay marriage and everything in between.
title: A Night in Vegas

description: Like a disturbing sore, “Puppetry of the Penis” returns to terroritze your genitals. It's all in the title: two men use their dicks for what they call “genital origami.” That is, they stretch, twist, tie, and distort their little men into various shapes, all while keeping up a comedic patter.
title: Puppetry of the Penis

description: A car accident involving a wolf acts as the catalyst for a trio of young men and women. “Wolves” sounds like a good, well-made drama crammed with the substance of American life, created and produced by an intelligent (and handsome) crew of hungry, idealistic young artists.
title: Wolves

description: A revival of last year’s luminous import from Britain, based on a play by Noel Coward and a film by David Lean
title: Brief Encounter

description: A British play about miners who become artists, from the writer of “Billy Elliot”
title: The Pitmen Painters

description: David Mamet’s backstage drama sees a veteran actor (Patrick Stewart) eclipsed by a young talent (TR Knight)
title: Schoenfeld TheaterA Life in the Theater

description: A revival of the Off-Broadway hit emo-rock musical about our seventh president, full of youth and attitude
title: Bloody Bloody Andrew Jackson

description: A return of last season’s Broadway sleeper drama: war journalists find a quiet life on the home front unbearable
title: Time Stands Still

description: This comedy smash from London pits a classical dramatist (David Hyde Pierce) against a clown (Mark Rylance)
title: La Bete

description: A biodrama about football coaching legend Vince Lombardi (Dan Luria)
title: Lombardi

description: The Pulitzer/Oscar winner makes its Broadway debut with James Earl Jones chauffeuring Vanessa Redgrave
title: Driving Miss Daisy

description: A new musical about a famous miscarriage of justice in the 1930s, by the creators of “Chicago”
title: The Scottsboro Boys

description: Al Pacino kills as Shylock in this revival of Will Shakespeare’s masterpiece, revived after this summer’s run
title: The Merchant of Venice

description: A multimedia concert that mingles historical footage of the Fab Four with a quartet of impersonators
title: Rain: A Tribute to the Beatles

description: A glossy production about a sexually voracious, wealthy black man living in 1802 New Orleans
title: A Free Man of Color

description: A stageshow version of the classic Saturday morning TV series, starring a man-child & his wonderful toys
title: The Pee-Wee Herman Show

description: A musical adaptation of the Will Ferrell comedy about a man who becomes one of Santa’s elves
title: Elf

description: By Brad White "Model Homes and Habitats" a contemporary art exhibit focused on wildlife welfare. Ends Oct. 18.
title: Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest

description:
Via the organizers:

What makes men do the things they do? Why do women so often end up as collateral damage in their struggle to prove their manhood? The Wreckless Stage Company presents the world premiere of Viewer Discretion Advised, a contemporary psychological thriller which tackles these questions. In this startling contemporary drama, a seemingly casual encounter between strangers Norm and Bud slowly reveals a menacingly dangerous play for power and ruthless competition for Norm’s girlfriend Anne. Playwright Ed Stevens explores what happens when "men behaving badly" spirals out of control, forcing the characters to confront how far they will go to prove themselves to one another. “Conjured a vividly distinct world in this play, enshrouded in an ever-darkening atmosphere of anxiety and unease”— Steppenwolf Theatre "An excellent job of developing an increasingly perilous plot with tremendous humor and well-crafted dialogue” – Goodman Theatre
title: Viewer Discretion Advised
