description:
Via the organizers:

The Prentices are not an ordinary couple. Dr. Prentice is a psychiatrist with his own hospital who believes that the best way to interview a girl for a job is to seduce her. Geraldine Barclay does her best to comply, but nothing is going to work smoothly in this nut house that includes Mrs. Prentice, a nymphomaniac who is seduced by a bellhop in a hotel, or maybe it’s vice versa. Mrs. Prentice brings home her reluctant bellhop just as the state inspector decides to pay a visit to the hospital. What ensues is a wild melee of disappearances, disguises and discoveries as husband and wife try to hide their prizes from the inspector and from one another. What the Butler Saw premiered in London's West End in 1969, two years after rising star playwright Orton was bludgeoned to death with a hammer by his male lover at the age of 34. The play has never had a Broadway production.
title: What the Butler Saw

description: In this departure from Dickens, Scrooge's famous tale of redemption and gentle grace is placed squarely on its head and The Ghost of Christmas Past has enough attitude to portray all three spirits. She to show Scrooge his past, present and future in order to change him, but her magic keeps malfunctioning in Durang's version, and they consistently find themselves transported to the wrong time and place. She tries to take Scrooge back to the past, but instead she and Scrooge keep appearing in the present at the Cratchit's home. Mrs. Bob Cratchit, taking center stage here, is no longer loving and long-suffering. Rather Mrs. Bob is in a rage. She is sick of Tiny Tim (the goody-goody crippled child), she hates her 20 other children (most of them confined to the root cellar), including oversized Little Nell, and she wants to get drunk and jump off London Bridge. As the Ghost loses more control, the plot morphs into parodies of Oliver Twist, "The Gift of the Magi" and It's a Wonderful Life. And that's before Scrooge and Mrs. Bob start falling in love.

description:
(Credit: Simon Crowe)

The Furman University Theatre Arts Department has worked and performed in a tiny, “temporary” building since the late 1960’s, but that hasn’t stopped the school’s faculty and students from tackling an ambitious slate of both new and classic plays.

This month brings Tom Stoppard’s “Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are Dead,” a revisionist take on “Hamlet” in which the Danish Prince’s two school friends are the title characters. Rosencrantz (Ben Montague) and Guildenstern (Jake Parker) are charged to bring Hamlet (John Tate) to his death in England; this episode occurs offstage in Shakespeare’s play but in Stoppard’s hands is a darkly funny meditation on fate and the futility of trying to understand one’s place in the world.

Don’t be intimidated if you’re not a “Hamlet” scholar; cast member Mary Beth Smith says that although Stoppard’s play deals with universal and important themes that “the fun will come through” for audiences.

Director Jay Oney was a cast member when Furman last produced “Rosencrantz & Guildenstern” back in 1977. Oney is now a faculty member who says he has “unfinished business” with the play as he talks about the excitement and difficulties of directing his all-student cast. There’s plenty of subtext for lead actors Parker, Montague, and Andy Brame (as The Player King) to chew on but in order to make the most out of his rehearsal time Oney puts a good deal of responsibility on the actors to develop characters on their own. Rehearsals can’t focus too much on any one cast member since the play is full of physical comedy (a key scene involves the switching of a letter while Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are asleep) which must be carefully choreographed both to ensure maximum laughs and for the actors’ safety.

Furman University has been a quiet fixture on the Greenville theater scene, producing plays continuously in the same building for more than 40 years. If you’ve never seen a play at Furman, don’t be scared. Oney says the school’s tiny 110-seat Playhouse is “the best place to watch a play in town,” and if physical proximity to the actors is your thing, then both “Rosencrantz and Guildenstern” and the building it’s performed in are worth the price of admission.

—Simon Crowe, Special to Metromix
title: “Rosencrantz and Guildenstern”

description:
Everybody’s favorite musical from the 80s is back, with a local flavor. Greenville Little Theatre will host “Little Shop of Horrors” Sept. 17-Oct. 3, so get ready to sing along to some of your favorite show tunes.

For those who’ve never seen it, this rock musical, a spoof of classic B-movies, tells the tale of a woebegone florist shop worker who grows a plant that feeds on human blood. Packed with doo-wop, rock ‘n’ roll and Motown tunes, the show had a long run off-Broadway from 1982 through 1987.

The Greenville Little Theatre productions will show on Fridays and Saturdays at 8 p.m. and Sundays at 3 p.m. Tickets cost $30 and can be purchased at the box office or by calling 864-233-6238. For more information, visit www.greenvillelittletheatre.org.
title: 'Little Shop of Horrors'

description:
It’s a classic rock-opera and has a cult-like following. If you’re one of the ones with a special place in your heart for “The Rocky Horror Show,” mark your calendar for Oct. 15. That’s when the rock opera will begin its run at Warehouse Theatre, complete with a dazzling local cast.

Talented local actor Will Ragland will take on the infamous role of the bizarre Dr. Frank-N-Furter, with whom two engaged lovebirds seek refuge after their car breaks down in a remote area. Ragland has earned local fame from his appearances in musical productions such as Centre Stage’s super-popular “Buddy: The Buddy Holly Story.”

“The Rocky Horror Show” will run through Oct. 31, with performances on Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. Showtime is at 8 p.m. except on Sundays, when the performances start at 3 p.m. Tickets are $25 for adults and $15 for students, and can be ordered in advance by calling 864-235-6948 or purchased in person at the box office. For more information, visit www.warehousetheatre.com.
title: "The Rocky Horror Show"

description: "Rounding Third" introduces two little league coaches—one a veteran, the other a new recruit—and their markedly different philosophies about the game of baseball. This romantic comedy captures the same heartfelt warmth as the author's blockbuster hit, Driving Miss Daisy.

description:
Shadowbox Cabaret is putting out another original musical, but this time it's the musical documentary, "Back to the Garden," re-opening Sunday, September 26, at their Easton Town Center theater. 

The show tells the story of the Woodstock Music and Art Fair with original scenes mixed with quotes from key performers and songs from the concert itself. 

Shadowobx's head writer, Jimmy Mak, stars as fictional New York Times reporter Rodney Benton who is covering the music festival for his paper. Benton interacts with real-life concert producers Mike Lang, Artie Kornfield (portrayed by Robbie Nance and Andrew Cioffi), emcee Chip Monck (portrayed by David Whitehouse), activist Abbie Hoffman (portrayed by Brett McCardle), and "Hog Farmer" Hugh Romney a.k.a. Wavy Gravy (portrayed by Andy Ankrom), as well as the producer's fictional assistant "Serena" played by Amy Lay. 

Mak based the Benton character on real life report Barnard Collier and stayed true to many documented stories surrounding the famous concert. 

"Back to the Garden" runs 2:30 pm. and 7 p.m. Sunday nights. (Doors open at 6.) Tickets are $30 for adults and $20 for students and seniors. To purchase reservations contact the Shadowbox box office at 614-416-7625 or visit www.shadowboxcabaret.com.
title: 'Back to the Garden' presented by Shadowbox

description: Born the son of a former Mississippi slave, Elijah Pierce migrated north in the early 1900s and settled in Columbus to become a preacher, barbershop owner, and one of America's most celebrated folk artists. "Pierce to the Soul," a world premiere written by Columbus playwright Chiquita Mullins Lee, celebrates this hometown hero, his struggles, his triumphs, and the vibrant life that swirled around him in Columbus for more than 50 years.
title: 'Pierce to the Soul' by CATCO

description: In this stunning one-woman show, Eleni Papaleonardos steers us through the evolution of human communication, her life-long dance with dyslexia, and the Esperanto of street signs, finally driving head-first into the ever-daunting gap between language and meaning. Directed by John Dranschak and Jeanine Thompson.
title: Available Light Theatre presents 'Stop Sign Language'

description: Taking a page from the Saturday Nigh Live playbook, Sunday Night Players is the only lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender sketch comedy troupe in Central Ohio. They take to the stage the last Sunday of every month at Wall Street Night Club with original skits solely created by the troupe. Every May they also host a pretty extravagant fundraiser for breast cancer awareness (all proceeds benefit the Susan G. Komen foundation). And their September show is dedicated to raising money for autism research. We definitely recommend you call Wall Street to reserve a table as their shows tend to sell out pretty quickly.
title: Sunday Night Players at Wall Street

description: Fishnet Mafia hosts the city's only traditional midnight shadow cast showing of "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" the first Saturday of every month at Studio 35. Concessions and beer are available (with PBRs going for only $2). Come prepared as the traditional callbacks are welcome. Prop bas are also sold for $1. And kisses with the cast are even for sale! Each month has a different theme, making the Rocky Horror experience a different one every time. It's definitely a monthly event that can't be missed.
title: 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' by Fishnet Mafia

description:
Before you know it, hot, humid days will give way to cool, crisp nights, and the kids will head back to school. As autumn approaches, the Shadowbox metaperformers get mischievous, and that means audiences can look forward to a fiendishly fun entertainment experience with "Nightmare at Shadowbox Live!"
 
Shadowbox turns tricks and treats into fright night with it's newest theme, "Nightmare at Shadowbox Live," running September 2 through November 13 at the Easton Town Center. Original sketch comedy and live rock 'n' roll will give you thrills, chills, and a glimpse into the dreamscape we call nightmares.
 
"Nightmare at Shadowbox Live" runs 7:30 p.m. Thursdays; 7:30 p.m. and 10:30 p.m. Fridays and Saturdays. Tickets are $30 for adults and $20 for students/seniors.  For more information and reservations call the Shadowbox box office at 614-416-7625 or visit ShadowboxLive.org.
title: Nightmare at Shadowbox Live

description:
In this world premiere musical by Tony nominee Bill Russell ("Side Show") and Drama Desk nominee Peter Melnick ("Adrift in Macao"), smoking has been outlawed in America, but Pam is finding it impossible to quit. Her struggle is complicated by husband Ernie, who dreams of being a rock star, and their teenage son Jimmy, who listens to so much rap music he's convinced he's black. Meanwhile their nosy, evangelistic, anti-smoking neighbor Phyllis lurks around every corner trying to catch Pam mid-puff. Will Pam kick the habit or fight for the right to light up as "The Last Smoker in America?" Columbus will be the first to find out in this original, raucous, irreverent musical.

Tickets go onsale Aug. 19 and the four-week run is expected to sell out so get your tickets early! Call 614-469-0939 or visit CATCO.org.
venue: Studio One Theatre at Vern Riffe Center
title: 'The Last Smoker in America'

description:
Warning: This play contains violence, profanity, raw content and is advised for adult audiences ONLY.

Topdog/Underdog tells the story of two brothers, Lincoln (Moses Goods) and Booth (Q), who, abandoned by both parents, have had to depend upon each other for survival since they were teenagers. Now in their thirties, the brothers struggle to make a new life, one that will lead them out of poverty. Lincoln, a master of the con game three-card monte, has abandoned a life of crime for a more respectable job impersonating Abraham Lincoln at an arcade. Booth, on the other hand, earns his living as a petty thief, one who wishes to emulate his older brother’s success by learning how to “throw the cards.” Throughout the play, the brothers compete against each other, vying for control. At any given moment, one may yield power over the other, only to relinquish it in the next. Topdog/Underdog reveals a topsy-turvy world in which Lincoln and Booth live, a chaotic world that is as dangerous as it is illusory.
title: Topdog/Underdog

description:
Fake Bacon Productions brings you "Comedytown" at the Gateway Film Center. Occurring on the first and third Fridays of every month, Fake Bacon Productions will present improv-based comedy in two fun formats, Comedy Town Improv and Comedytown Showdown.
 
Comedytown Improv will take place on the first Friday of each month. Fake Bacon will collaborate with The Shimmy Shake Project and other special guests from top local improv troupes to perform this monthly shortform improv show.

Comedytown Showdown will take place on the third Friday of each month. Fake Bacon will collaborate with The Shimmy Shake Project, guest improvisers, and local stand-up comedians to perform this fast-paced monthly show featuring a comedy “competition” between two teams of intermingled improv performers and stand-up comedians. The audience will decide the winners of a series of comedy battles to crown the ultimate showdown champion.
title: 'Comedytown' at Gateway Film Center
